title: Dominic and the Hymn
premise: Bram Kavanagh takes a teaching post in the fog-bound town of Hollowmere, where students vanish one by one and every adult insists they simply moved away. When Bram's childhood imaginary friend, Dominic, appears on their porch — unchanged after thirty years — Bram learns the disappearances are tied to a hymn the town sings at every assembly, a song that must never be finished. The missing children are trapped inside the song's unfinished final verse, held there by the choir master who wrote it to keep his drowned son 'safe' forever. To free them, Bram and Dominic must learn the last verse without singing it aloud, confront the choir master in the flooded chapel beneath the school, and choose between loyalty to the friend who saved Bram's childhood and the truth that Dominic is himself a fragment of the song. In the end Bram sings the verse alone, voice cracking but unaccompanied, releasing the children and unmaking Dominic — who fades smiling, finally allowed to end.
about_author: Emrys Eastwick is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years counting heads in classrooms that never quite added up. They write horror about institutions, small towns, and the things children know that adults agree to forget.

chapters.title: Head Count
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram arrives in Hollowmere, takes the teaching post, and notices the attendance ledger has more crossed-out names than living students. The vice principal warns them to keep doors counted and lights on. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity masked as professional diligence.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A student named Wren doesn't return after half-term; her desk is removed overnight as if she never existed. Bram finds her half-finished essay describing 'the pretty song under the floor.' Emotional beat: first real dread, and the decision not to look away.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The whole school sings the Hymn of Hollowmere; Bram feels the melody pull at something wordless in their chest and stops singing mid-verse. The choir master, Mr. Aldous Vane, watches them with cold interest. Emotional beat: the sense of being marked.

chapters.title: Porch Light
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. On a rain-lashed night, Dominic is waiting on the porch — exactly as he looked when Bram was seven: same patched coat, same too-wide smile. He says he's been looking for them for thirty years. Emotional beat: terror braided with unbearable tenderness.

chapters.title: Rules We Made
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, flashbacks to childhood. Dominic explains he can only appear where the song is sung, and warns Bram never to learn the words past the third verse. Bram tests him with questions only the real Dominic could answer. Emotional beat: cautious rekindled trust.

chapters.title: The Mothers of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram interviews parents of the missing; each repeats identical phrases about children 'going somewhere better.' One mother breaks down and hums three notes before clamping her mouth shut. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into compliance.

chapters.title: Found Family, Found Again
chapters.summary: Alternating Bram and Dominic POVs. Dominic meets Bram's neighbor, teenage outcast Sefa, who can hear him — the first person besides Bram ever to do so. The three form an unlikely circle over burnt toast and ghost stories. Emotional beat: warmth, fragile and defiant.

chapters.title: Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa sneaks into the school basement and hears children's voices harmonizing beneath the boiler room floor. She records it on her phone; the recording plays back only silence and one word: soon. Emotional beat: brave, foolish escalation.

chapters.title: Vane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram breaks into the choir master's office and finds forty years of attendance books, each vanished child's name annotated with a musical notation instead of a date. The oldest entry is a boy named Tobias Vane, 1983. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: What Dominic Won't Say
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic remembers being sung into existence by a lonely boy beside a flooded quarry, and knows what he is — but hides it from Bram, terrified of losing them. He lies for the first time in their long friendship. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling toward betrayal.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following water stains and old blueprints, Bram finds a sealed chapel beneath the school's east wing, its pews facing a drained baptismal font shaped like a music staff. Wet footprints lead in; none lead out. Emotional beat: awe tipping into horror.

chapters.title: Verse Four
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa discovers a hymnal with the fourth verse torn from every copy in town — except one hidden in the library's local history section, written in a child's careful hand. She memorizes it before she understands what it costs. Emotional beat: the thrill of forbidden knowledge.

chapters.title: Wren, Singing
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Wren appears briefly in the school corridor, translucent, mouthing the melody, pointing down. She can only manifest where the hymn was sung loudest. Bram realizes the missing aren't gone — they're held. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Aldous Vane Confesses
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane recounts drowning his son Tobias in the quarry in 1983 and writing the hymn so the boy would be 'kept safe in the song forever.' Every vanished child since has joined the chorus keeping Tobias company. Emotional beat: monstrous grief, sincerely felt.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Vane offers Bram a trade: leave Hollowmere and forget, or join the search party below. He reveals he knows about Dominic — 'You've been carrying a piece of my song since you were a child.' Emotional beat: the ground giving way beneath everything Bram trusts.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Bram and Dominic, alternating POVs. Bram confronts Dominic, who admits he was born from the hymn's first singing and cannot exist if the song ends. Bram must choose: keep Dominic forever or free the children. Emotional beat: heartbreak at full volume.

chapters.title: Doors Counted, Lights Out
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Vane locks down the school during a storm assembly, intending to sing the full hymn with the whole student body and take everyone at once. Sefa cuts the power and opens every door, buying chaos. Emotional beat: found family fighting like a single animal.

chapters.title: Down Into the Verse
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram descends into the flooded chapel with Dominic and Sefa, following Wren's voice through knee-deep black water to find the missing children standing in rows, singing without breath. Emotional beat: dread transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Climax. Bram's POV. Before Vane's assembled choir above, Bram sings the final verse alone — unaccompanied, unsanctioned — while Dominic holds the chapel door against Vane. The song resists, tries to make Bram harmonize; they force the words out solo. Emotional beat: defiance as an act of love.

chapters.title: Unmaking
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. As the verse completes, the children wake and wade toward light. Dominic begins to unravel, note by note, and chooses not to fight it. He tells Bram he was always the part of them that survived. Emotional beat: devastating, grateful farewell.

chapters.title: After the Amen
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Vane, emptied by the loss of his song, walks into the old quarry. The children are returned; the town pretends nothing happened, but the mothers stop humming. Bram keeps teaching, keeps counting heads — and now every name answers. Emotional beat: exhausted, imperfect peace.

chapters.title: Someone New on the Porch
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Bram's POV. Months later, a new student tells Bram about her imaginary friend, and Bram teaches her the important rule: some friends are real, and some songs should stay unfinished. On the porch that night, no one is waiting — and Bram smiles anyway. Emotional beat: grief integrated, love carried forward.
